references.relationship: CLRA §1770(a)(14) is automatically violated by any Rees-Levering violation (representing that a transaction involves rights/remedies/obligations that it does not). Plead together: Rees-Levering supplies forfeiture, CLRA supplies damages + notice-and-cure mechanism.

UCL 'unlawful' prong: every Rees-Levering violation is a UCL predicate. 4-year SOL preserves claims that fall outside Rees-Levering's shorter limitations period. Restitution + injunctive relief available.

Song-Beverly Consumer Warranty Act. Pleaded alongside Rees-Levering when the vehicle itself is defective in addition to the paperwork being non-compliant. Different remedy: buyback / civil penalty for willful violation.

Rosenthal Act attaches to downstream debt collection after a non-compliant Rees-Levering sale. If a dealer or assignee pursues collection despite forfeiture, the collection itself may be an actionable misrepresentation.
Common-law deceit substrate. Rees-Levering supplements but does not displace common-law fraud. Punitive damages via Civ §3294 available on deceit theory without CLRA §1782 notice prerequisite.
FCRA federal parallel for credit reporting consequences of auto fraud cases. When a dealer reports a non-compliant loan as a delinquency, FCRA dispute procedures apply.

incorporated_federal_authorities: 16 CFR §433.2 (FTC Holder Rule) — makes assignee subject to consumer defenses
